14:25 Local Time, 12:25 GMT, 17:55 IST: South Africa have completed a comprehensive victory to seal the series 2-0, and they were never on the back foot in this Test. Right from the toss, which stand-in skipper Aiden Markram won before opting to bowl, the hosts had things going their way. Their bowlers made the most of the conditions on a rain-affected opening day, bundling Bangladesh out for a paltry 91. The batters then took full advantage of the good batting conditions on Day 2, with Marques Ackerman's superb 150 and Wiaan Mulder's fifth Test hundred powering them to 494/7 and a massive 403-run lead. South Africa declared at the start of Day 3, leaving Bangladesh with a mountain to climb. The visitors began their second innings positively, with the openers putting together a 58-run stand, but once that was broken, the wickets began to fall at regular intervals.

There was a brief fightback through a 50-run partnership between Towhid Hridoy and Najmul Hossain Shanto, but Rabada broke that stand before Wiaan Mulder took over. Mulder ran through the lower middle order, picking up his career-best Test figures (7/31) to go with that century earlier in the match. Bangladesh had begun the post-lunch session three wickets down, but Mulder's spell ensured they were bowled out inside two sessions on the third day itself. A thoroughly dominant performance from South Africa, who take giant strides in the WTC points table and consolidate their top spot. Stay with us for the presentations..

Markram (2/3): [On the strength and depth of the South African bowling attack] Yeah, it's a big blessing. I'm sure Temba will say the same thing when you're captaining a bowling attack like that going late into the game as well. You've got Harmy and Wiaan doing their thing. You're blessed with many options. So long may they stay on the park for South Africa. And yeah, from a captain's point of view, it's a delight having them. [On batting alongside Marques Ackerman and his impact on the team] Yeah, it's great. Brings a lot of energy, obviously takes the game on in his own natural way. So I've watched just from the Australia series into this one how he's owned his own approach to Test cricket has been really heartwarming for the lot watching up top. And he's putting guys under pressure and doing that creates sort of bad balls and he's putting those away. So incredibly chuffed for him. He's done it the long, hard way and it's really great to see a guy like that succeed at this level.

Markram collects the trophy and goes to his team mates standing behind the CHAMPIONS board. Even Temba Bavuma is there and Markram hands him the trophy, and he then lifts it up. The confetti goes up and there are a few photographs taken before the coaching staff joins the celebrations.

Bangladesh will look back at that first Test as an opportunity missed. They put up 400 batting first but failed to capitalise, conceding a 157-run lead and allowing South Africa to take control of the contest. From there, the visitors largely played catch-up and never quite managed to turn things around. As for South Africa, this is a welcome return to winning ways after opening their home summer with a defeat to Australia. They made a few changes following that loss, and one of the biggest positives to emerge has been the discovery of a gem in Marques Ackerman. He's taken to Test cricket like a duck to water, with two hundreds and two fifties in his first six innings. He'll certainly be one to watch when South Africa take on England in the three-Test series next month. And that brings us to the end of our coverage. We hope you enjoyed every bit of the action.
